newsitem.title: USA: Amtran unit to cut 15 pct of workforce.
newsitem.headline: Amtran unit to cut 15 pct of workforce.

text.p: Amtran Inc said Friday its American Trans Air (ATA) principal subsidiary will reduce its overall workforce by about 15 percent over the next two months.
Amtran said the reductions will be made through discontinuance of outside contractors, elimination of part-time employees, and layoffs.

It added the majority of the staff reductions will impact employees at locations where ATA previously has announced scheduled service cutbacks, as well as employees at the corporate headquarters who support those routes.
Hourly and salaried workers at all levels of the company will be affected, Amtran sid.

Previously, Amtran said it will phase out scheduled service from Boston by early December. The company also has announced plans to eliminate selected unprofitable destinations and reduce its schedule within Florida.
Amtran said these plans leave ATA,s most attractive routes intact, and the company plans in the future to build upon its success in these markets.
ATA serves vacation destinations from Indianapolis, Milwaukee and Chicago's Midway Airport with charter and scheduled flights.
In a statement, Stanley Pace, Amtran president, said increased competition and unattractive financial performance on certain routes were the primary reasons for the reductions in scheduled service.
The company also plans to reallocate some of its planes to its charter segment. Amtran said ATA is the largest charter carrier in the United States.
